Board

Pure-logic board holding terrain layout (Width, Height, Terrains, and a per-tile terrain key grid). Units and obstacles are not stored here; callers overlay them as blocked/ally sets when querying range and paths.

Board.Width

public int Width { get; }

Type: int

Board.Height

Gets the board height in tiles.

public int Height { get; }

Type: int

Board.Terrains

Gets the terrain definitions keyed by terrain key.

public IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TerrainType> Terrains { get; }

Type: IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TerrainType>

Board constructor

Initializes a board filled with the default terrain.

public Board(int width, int height, string defaultTerrain, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TerrainType> terrains)
Parameter Type Description
width int The board width in tiles.
height int The board height in tiles.
defaultTerrain string The terrain key filling every tile.
terrains IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TerrainType> The terrain definitions keyed by terrain key.

Board.InBounds

Returns true when the point lies inside the board bounds.

public bool InBounds(GridPoint p)
Parameter Type Description
p GridPoint The point to test.

public TerrainType GetTerrain(GridPoint p)
Parameter Type Description
p GridPoint The point to read.

Board.FromRows

Builds a board from ASCII rows where each character maps through the legend, throwing on ragged rows or unknown glyphs.

public static Board FromRows(string[] rows, string defaultTerrain, IDictionary<char, string> legend, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, TerrainType> terrains)
Parameter Type Description
rows string[] The ASCII rows with one character per tile.
defaultTerrain string The terrain key filling the board before glyphs are applied.
legend IDictionary<char, string> The map from glyph character to terrain key (BMP characters only).

public override bool Equals(object? obj)

Movement class. Drives per-terrain move costs (fliers ignore most terrain).

Infantry 0 Standard foot movement.

Cavalry 2 Mounted movement.

MovementGroups.Armor

html:
API: SrpgCore.Random

Generated from ../SrpgCore sources by scripts/build-api.ts — do not edit by hand.

Guide: overview.

SeededRng

Deterministic RNG (xorshift32). One stream per battle/level, constructed from a saved seed, so forecasts, AI, replays and tests all share one reproducible sequence. Not for security use.

SeededRng constructor

Creates a deterministic stream from the given seed.

public SeededRng(uint seed)
Parameter Type Description
seed uint Starting seed, with zero replaced by a fixed nonzero fallback.

SeededRng.NextUInt

Advances the xorshift32 stream and returns the next word.

public uint NextUInt()

Returns: uint — Next unsigned value in the deterministic sequence.

SeededRng.GetState

Snapshot the stream for saves/turnwheel; restore with SetState.

public uint GetState()

Returns: uint — Current internal stream state.

SeededRng.SetState

Restores a snapshot taken by GetState.

public void SetState(uint state)
Parameter Type Description
state uint Stream state to resume, with zero replaced by a fixed fallback.

SeededRng.CreateStream

Independent sub-stream (combat/growth/other split): combat rolls never shift growth rolls. Same (baseSeed, streamIndex) always yields the same stream.

public static SeededRng CreateStream(uint baseSeed, uint streamIndex)
Parameter Type Description
baseSeed uint Shared base seed for the level or battle.
streamIndex uint Per-concern index splitting combat from growth and other streams.

Returns: SeededRng — Independent deterministic stream for one concern.

SeededRng.Next

Returns the next bounded integer from the stream.

public int Next(int exclusiveUpperBound)
Parameter Type Description
exclusiveUpperBound int Exclusive upper bound, must be positive.

Returns: int — Integer in [0, exclusiveUpperBound).

SeededRng.NextDouble

Returns the next uniform double from the stream.

public double NextDouble()

Returns: double — Double in [0, 1).

SeededRng.RollHit1RN

Classic single-roll hit check against a 0-100 rate.

public bool RollHit1RN(int hitRate)
Parameter Type Description
hitRate int Hit rate from 0 to 100 with absolute endpoints.

Returns: bool — True when the single 0-99 roll falls below the rate.

SeededRng.RollHit2RN

GBA-style 2RN: averages two 0-99 rolls, which skews outcomes toward the displayed rate (high hit feels reliable, low hit feels hopeless). This is the Fire Emblem feel.

public bool RollHit2RN(int hitRate)
Parameter Type Description
hitRate int Hit rate from 0 to 100 with absolute endpoints.

Returns: bool — True when the mean of two 0-99 rolls falls below the rate.

EnemyAi

Greedy enemy brain with lethality-first scoring: (1) strike from current tile, (2) move then strike, (3) approach nearest foe. Enumerates every usable weapon across every reachable tile and foe. Terrain-aware when a terrain lookup is supplied; otherwise all bonuses read 0. Counter-risk is subtracted as expected counter damage times CounterWeight (0 = ignore, 1 = full). Pass a SupportLedger to weight bonded hit/avoid bonuses into both the strike and the counter-risk forecasts. Deterministic: ties break by least movement spent then nearest target then move tile foe nid and weapon key.

Phase-boundary upkeep for one team: terrain HP swing, then poison damage, then a status tick per unit, in deterministic coordinate order (X, then Y — the same order EnemyAi enumerates tiles). Hosts call Apply when a team's phase begins; per-unit report is (nid, total hpDelta, expired status names). Pure predicates over unit state; the TurnManager/event layer decides when to poll (after every elimination checkpoint; survive only on turn advance). Objectives.IsRouted Rout completes when no live unit of a side remains. public static bool IsRouted(IEnumerable<Unit> units, Affiliation side) Parameter Type Description units IEnumerable<Unit> Units to scan for survivors. side Affiliation Side tested for elimination. Returns: bool — True when that side has no live unit left. Objectives.HasSurvived "Survive N" completes N full rounds: victory once TurnNumber passes N. public static bool HasSurvived(int turnNumber, int turnsToSurvive) Parameter Type Description turnNumber int Current turn number (starts at 1). turnsToSurvive int Full rounds that must complete. Returns: bool — True once the required rounds have elapsed. Objectives.IsProtectFailed Protect fails when a listed tag (unit nid) is dead AND already spawned. Future spawns (spawnTurn > turnNumber) never trip it. Use <= (not ==) for spawn comparison: skipped turn numbers must not drop the check. public static bool IsProtectFailed(IEnumerable<Unit> units, IEnumerable<string> tags, int turnNumber, Func<string, int> spawnTurnOf) Parameter Type Description units IEnumerable<Unit> Units keyed by nid for liveness lookup. tags IEnumerable<string> Protected unit nids to check. turnNumber int Current turn number for the spawned comparison. spawnTurnOf Func<string, int> Maps a tag to its spawn turn. Returns: bool — True when a spawned protected unit is dead or missing. Objectives.IsSeized Seize succeeds when the listed unit is alive and standing on the region. Pure over placements; the caller resolves the region by name. public static bool IsSeized(IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> placed, string unitNid, Regions.Region region) Parameter Type Description placed IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> Placements scanned for the seizing unit. unitNid string Nid of the unit that must seize the region. region Regions.Region Region the unit must stand on. Returns: bool — True when that live unit stands on the region. Objectives.IsEscape Escape succeeds when the listed unit is alive and standing on the escape region. Mirrors seize semantics; LT Maker escape is reaching a designated region alive. public static bool IsEscape(IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> placed, string unitNid, Regions.Region region) Parameter Type Description placed IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> Placements scanned for the escaping unit. unitNid string Nid of the unit that must escape through the region. region Regions.Region Escape region the unit must stand on. Returns: bool — True when that live unit stands on the escape region. PhaseTickRules Tunable phase-boundary attrition. Values: PoisonDamage per poisoned unit, RegenHeal per regenerating unit, TickStatuses toggle, ApplyTerrain toggle. PhaseTickRules.PoisonDamage HP lost per poisoned unit per tick (GBA-flavored default). public int PoisonDamage { get; set; } Type: int PhaseTickRules.RegenHeal HP gained per regenerating unit per tick. public int RegenHeal { get; set; } Type: int PhaseTickRules.TickStatuses Decrement status durations and report expirations. public bool TickStatuses { get; set; } Type: bool PhaseTickRules.ApplyTerrain Apply per-tile TerrainEffects (fort heal, marsh damage). public bool ApplyTerrain { get; set; } Type: bool PhaseTick Phase-boundary upkeep for one team: terrain HP swing, then poison damage, then a status tick per unit, in deterministic coordinate order (X, then Y — the same order EnemyAi enumerates tiles). Hosts call Apply when a team's phase begins; per-unit report is (nid, total hpDelta, expired status names). Ticks never kill: a unit alive at tick start is left at 1 HP minimum; combat and objectives remain the only deaths. Skips dead units. Turn pipeline order: PhaseTick.Apply then SpawnDue (less or equal) then EvaluateObjectives then AI or input. Traps and events run as an explicit post-action stage after the commit. PhaseTick.Apply Runs phase-boundary upkeep for one team: terrain swing, poison, status ticks. public static List<(string nid, int hpDelta, string[] expiredStatuses)> Apply(ChapterState state, string team, PhaseTickRules? rules = null) Parameter Type Description state ChapterState Live chapter runtime (mutates HP and status durations). team string Team name (player, enemy, ally, other). rules PhaseTickRules? Toggles for terrain, poison damage, and status ticks. Returns: List<(string nid, int hpDelta, string[] expiredStatuses)> — Per-unit (nid, total hpDelta, expired status names) in tick order. ReplayHash Deterministic hash of chapter runtime for replay verification. ReplayHash.Compute Computes a deterministic hash of placements, HP, vars, RNG states, and skill catalog. public static string Compute(ChapterState state) Parameter Type Description state ChapterState Chapter runtime to hash. Returns: string — Hash string. Rescue Rescue (GBA simplify): a carrier grabs an adjacent non-hostile passenger whose Con fits (passenger Con <= carrier Con + 2), carries one at a time, moves at half MovePoints while carrying, and the passenger leaves the map (returns on drop). Rescued units are untargetable because they are not placed; hosts hide their tokens. Cross-side carries are refused: enemies block pass-through, so they can never be scooped either. Rescue.CanGrab Tests whether a carrier can grab an adjacent passenger. public static bool CanGrab(Unit carrier, Unit passenger, GridPoint carrierPos, GridPoint passengerPos) Parameter Type Description carrier Unit Unit attempting the grab (must have hands free). passenger Unit Unit to be carried (Con must fit). carrierPos GridPoint Current tile of the carrier. passengerPos GridPoint Current tile of the passenger. Returns: bool — True when adjacent, alive, same side, hands-free, and within Con capacity. Rescue.EffectiveMove Move allowance for a carrier, halved while carrying a passenger. public static int EffectiveMove(Unit carrier) Parameter Type Description carrier Unit Carrier whose allowance is computed (null reads as 0). Returns: int — Full move when unladen, half move when laden. Rescue.Grab Grab: records the carry and removes the passenger token. Returns the removed token. public static PlacedUnit Grab(Battlefield field, PlacedUnit carrier, PlacedUnit passenger) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield holding both tokens. carrier PlacedUnit Placed carrier doing the grabbing. passenger PlacedUnit Placed passenger being picked up. Returns: PlacedUnit — The removed passenger token for host bookkeeping. Rescue.Drop Drop the carried nid on an adjacent free tile. Needs the passenger Unit (hosts hold it). public static PlacedUnit Drop(Battlefield field, PlacedUnit carrier, Unit passenger, GridPoint tile) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield receiving the dropped passenger. carrier PlacedUnit Placed carrier doing the dropping. passenger Unit Passenger unit held by the host. tile GridPoint Adjacent free tile receiving the passenger. Returns: PlacedUnit — The newly deployed passenger token. UnitSnapshot Plain DTOs for saves/turnwheel/suspend (shape: Nid/Name/Side/ClassKey/Level/Experience/Stats/CurrentHP/MovePoints/MovementGroup/Vision/Skills/Statuses/Wexp/CarryingNid and Inventory keys with uses left). No JSON dependency: hosts serialize these with whatever they have. UnitSnapshot.Nid Unit nid key. public string Nid = ; Type: string UnitSnapshot.Name Display name. public string Name = ; Type: string UnitSnapshot.Side Side affiliation. public Affiliation Side; Type: Affiliation UnitSnapshot.ClassKey Class key. public string ClassKey = ; Type: string UnitSnapshot.Level Current level. public int Level; Type: int UnitSnapshot.Experience Accumulated experience toward the next level. public int Experience; Type: int UnitSnapshot.Stats Cloned stat block. public Stats Stats = new Stats(); Type: Stats UnitSnapshot.CurrentHP Current hit points. public int CurrentHP; Type: int UnitSnapshot.MovePoints Base movement allowance. public int MovePoints; Type: int UnitSnapshot.MovementGroup Movement group key for terrain costs. public string MovementGroup = ; Type: string UnitSnapshot.Vision Sight radius in Manhattan tiles. public int Vision = 5; Type: int UnitSnapshot.Skills Skill keys. public List<string> Skills = new List<string>(); Type: List<string> UnitSnapshot.Statuses Active statuses with remaining durations. public Dictionary<string, int> Statuses = new Dictionary<string, int>(); Type: Dictionary<string, int> UnitSnapshot.Wexp Weapon experience per weapon type. public Dictionary<WeaponType, int> Wexp = new Dictionary<WeaponType, int>(); Type: Dictionary<WeaponType, int> UnitSnapshot.CarryingNid Nid of the carried passenger (empty when hands-free). public string CarryingNid = ; Type: string UnitSnapshot.AiType AI type (rush/hold) persisted across saves. public string AiType = ; Type: string UnitSnapshot.PatrolA Patrol waypoint A for patrol AI. public GridPoint PatrolA; Type: GridPoint UnitSnapshot.PatrolB Patrol waypoint B for patrol AI. public GridPoint PatrolB; Type: GridPoint UnitSnapshot.Inventory Inventory as armory weapon keys with uses left. public List<InventorySnapshot> Inventory = new List<InventorySnapshot>(); Type: List<InventorySnapshot> InventorySnapshot One inventory entry for JSON-safe saves. InventorySnapshot.WeaponKey Armory weapon key. public string WeaponKey = ; Type: string InventorySnapshot.UsesLeft Uses remaining. public int UsesLeft; Type: int SupportPointSnapshot One support pair for JSON-safe saves. SupportPointSnapshot.A First nid. public string A = ; Type: string SupportPointSnapshot.B Second nid. public string B = ; Type: string SupportPointSnapshot.Points Accumulated points. public int Points; Type: int PlacedSnapshot Unit snapshot plus its board tile (Unit + X/Y). PlacedSnapshot.Unit Snapshot of the placed unit. public UnitSnapshot Unit = new UnitSnapshot(); Type: UnitSnapshot PlacedSnapshot.X Board X coordinate. public int X; Type: int PlacedSnapshot.Y Board Y coordinate. public int Y; Type: int SkillSnapshot One skill definition for save snapshot. SkillSnapshot.Id Skill id. public string Id = ; Type: string SkillSnapshot.Hook Hook side. public int Hook; Type: int SkillSnapshot.DamageBonus Damage bonus. public int DamageBonus; Type: int SkillSnapshot.HitBonus Hit bonus. public int HitBonus; Type: int SkillSnapshot.CritBonus Crit bonus. public int CritBonus; Type: int SkillSnapshot.DamageTakenPenalty Damage taken penalty. public int DamageTakenPenalty; Type: int SkillSnapshot.ProcChance Proc chance 0-100. public int ProcChance; Type: int ChapterSnapshot Full chapter save: TurnNumber/CurrentTeamIndex/BattleResult turn state, CombatRngState/GrowthRngState/ProcRngState, Vars flags, Placed placements with positions, and SpawnedNids to suppress re-spawns on restore. ChapterSnapshot.TurnNumber Turn number at save time. public int TurnNumber = 1; Type: int ChapterSnapshot.CurrentTeamIndex Index of the acting team at save time. public int CurrentTeamIndex; Type: int ChapterSnapshot.BattleResult Scripted battle result (null while ongoing). public bool? BattleResult; Type: bool? ChapterSnapshot.CombatRngState Saved combat RNG stream state. public uint CombatRngState; Type: uint ChapterSnapshot.GrowthRngState Saved growth RNG stream state. public uint GrowthRngState; Type: uint ChapterSnapshot.ProcRngState Saved proc RNG stream state. public uint ProcRngState; Type: uint ChapterSnapshot.Vars Chapter vars dictionary copy. public Dictionary<string, object?> Vars = new Dictionary<string, object?>(); Type: Dictionary<string, object?> ChapterSnapshot.Placed Placed unit snapshots. public List<PlacedSnapshot> Placed = new List<PlacedSnapshot>(); Type: List<PlacedSnapshot> ChapterSnapshot.SpawnedNids Already-spawned nids so restore never duplicates reinforcements. public List<string> SpawnedNids = new List<string>(); Type: List<string> ChapterSnapshot.Convoy Convoy items as weapon keys with uses left. public List<InventorySnapshot> Convoy = new List<InventorySnapshot>(); Type: List<InventorySnapshot> ChapterSnapshot.PartyGold Party gold for the shop (buy deducts, sell pays half). public int PartyGold; Type: int ChapterSnapshot.SupportPoints Support points per bonded pair. public List<SupportPointSnapshot> SupportPoints = new List<SupportPointSnapshot>(); Type: List<SupportPointSnapshot> ChapterSnapshot.SkillDefs Skill catalog snapshot. public List<SkillSnapshot> SkillDefs = new List<SkillSnapshot>(); Type: List<SkillSnapshot> ChapterSnapshot.Carried Rescued passengers held off-map. public List<UnitSnapshot> Carried = new List<UnitSnapshot>(); Type: List<UnitSnapshot> ChapterSnapshot.BoardWidth Board width in tiles for the terrain grid. public int BoardWidth; Type: int ChapterSnapshot.BoardHeight Board height in tiles for the terrain grid. public int BoardHeight; Type: int ChapterSnapshot.TerrainKeys Terrain keys in row major order. public List<string> TerrainKeys = new List<string>(); Type: List<string> SaveSystem Save/restore over a ChapterState. Units serialize fully (no template lookup on load); weapons resolve through chapter.Armory by key, so armory keys are the save contract. Deterministic: RNG stream states round-trip, so post-load rolls continue the sequence. SaveSystem.Save Snapshots positions, stats, inventory uses, turn state, vars, and RNG states. public static ChapterSnapshot Save(ChapterState state) Parameter Type Description state ChapterState Live chapter runtime to snapshot. Returns: ChapterSnapshot — Plain DTO snapshot the host can serialize. SaveSystem.Restore Rebuilds an equivalent chapter state from a snapshot; armory keys are the save contract. public static ChapterState Restore(Chapter chapter, ChapterSnapshot snap, uint baseSeed, IReadOnlyList<string>? teams = null) Parameter Type Description chapter Chapter Chapter providing board, armory, and event definitions. snap ChapterSnapshot Snapshot to restore. baseSeed uint Base seed for the fresh state before RNG states are applied. teams IReadOnlyList<string>? Phase order override (defaults to the chapter order). Returns: ChapterState — Live chapter state equivalent to the save point. Shove Adjacent shove/swap: pushes or exchanges adjacent units when Con/weight allows. Shove.CanShove True when shover can push target one tile away (adjacent, target destination free, Con sufficient). public static bool CanShove(Unit shover, Unit target, GridPoint shoverPos, GridPoint targetPos, Battlefield field) Parameter Type Description shover Unit Unit doing the shoving. target Unit Unit being shoved. shoverPos GridPoint Tile of the shover. targetPos GridPoint Tile of the target. field Battlefield Battlefield to test destination vacancy and bounds. Returns: bool — True when the push is legal. Shove.ExecuteShove Executes a shove: moves target one tile away from shover. public static void ExecuteShove(Battlefield field, PlacedUnit shover, PlacedUnit target) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield containing both units. shover PlacedUnit Placed shover. target PlacedUnit Placed target. Shove.CanSwap True when two adjacent units can swap positions. public static bool CanSwap(Unit a, Unit b, GridPoint aPos, GridPoint bPos) Parameter Type Description a Unit First unit. b Unit Second unit. aPos GridPoint Tile of first. bPos GridPoint Tile of second. Returns: bool — True when adjacent and both alive. Shove.ExecuteSwap Swaps positions of two adjacent placed units. public static void ExecuteSwap(PlacedUnit a, PlacedUnit b) Parameter Type Description a PlacedUnit First placed unit. b PlacedUnit Second placed unit. Steal GBA-style steal: adjacent thief with higher speed takes a light stealable item. Steal.CanSteal True when thief can steal weapon at slot from target. public static bool CanSteal(Unit thief, Unit target, GridPoint thiefPos, GridPoint targetPos, int weaponIndex) Parameter Type Description thief Unit Unit doing the stealing. target Unit Unit being stolen from. thiefPos GridPoint Thief tile. targetPos GridPoint Target tile. weaponIndex int Inventory index on target. Returns: bool — True when adjacent, alive, faster, and item light enough. Steal.Execute Moves inventory entry from target to thief. public static void Execute(Unit thief, Unit target, int weaponIndex) Parameter Type Description thief Unit Thief unit receiving the item. target Unit Target unit losing the item. weaponIndex int Slot on target. public static void Execute(Battlefield field, PlacedUnit thief, PlacedUnit target, string weaponKey) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield for position lookup. thief PlacedUnit Placed thief. target PlacedUnit Placed target. weaponKey string Weapon key to steal (first match). SupportRank Support rank between a pair of units (GBA C/B/A shape). Name Value Description None 0 No support bond. C 1 C rank (30 points, plus 5 hit and avoid). B 2 B rank (80 points, plus 10 hit and avoid). A 3 A rank (150 points, plus 15 hit and avoid). SupportLedger Adjacency support ledger: bonds keyed by ordered nid pair, points accumulate to ranks. Bonus: each bonded ally within 3 Manhattan tiles grants +5 hit/avoid per rank step (C +5, B +10, A +15), GBA-flavored. Pure over placements + ledger. Fork stacks additively across multiple bonded allies; GBA FE7/8 applies only the single highest support bonus in range. SupportLedger.PointsForRank Points threshold required to reach a rank. public static int PointsForRank(SupportRank rank) Parameter Type Description rank SupportRank Rank whose threshold is requested. Returns: int — Points needed for that rank (0 for None). SupportLedger.RankForPoints Derives the rank for an accumulated point total. public static SupportRank RankForPoints(int points) Parameter Type Description points int Accumulated bond points. Returns: SupportRank — Highest rank whose threshold is met. SupportLedger.AllPairs All bonded pairs with their accumulated points (for saves). public IEnumerable<((string a, string b) key, int points)> AllPairs() Returns: IEnumerable<((string a, string b) key, int points)> — Every canonical pair key with its point total. SupportLedger.SetPoints Restores points for a pair (for save restore). public void SetPoints(string a, string b, int points) Parameter Type Description a string First nid. b string Second nid. points int Points to restore. SupportLedger.AddPoints Accumulates bond points for an ordered pair (stored canonically). public void AddPoints(string a, string b, int points) Parameter Type Description a string First unit nid. b string Second unit nid. points int Points to add (non-positive values are ignored). SupportLedger.RankOf Reads the current rank for a unit pair. public SupportRank RankOf(string a, string b) Parameter Type Description a string First unit nid. b string Second unit nid. Returns: SupportRank — Rank for the pair (None when unbonded). SupportLedger.BonusForRank Hit and avoid bonus granted by one bond of a rank. public static int BonusForRank(SupportRank rank) Parameter Type Description rank SupportRank Bond rank. Returns: int — Five per rank step (C 5, B 10, A 15). SupportLedger.TickAdjacent Grants 1 support point per adjacent alive ally pair (GBA-flavored tick). public int TickAdjacent(Battlefield field) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield to read adjacency from. Returns: int — Number of pairs that gained a point. SupportLedger.BonusFor Sums hit and avoid from bonded allies within 3 Manhattan tiles (fork: additive stacking across allies; GBA uses single highest). public (int hit, int avoid) BonusFor(Unit unit, GridPoint pos, IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> allies) Parameter Type Description unit Unit Unit receiving the bonus. pos GridPoint Tile the unit is evaluated from. allies IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> Candidate bonded allies. Returns: (int hit, int avoid) — (hitBonus, avoidBonus) summed across all bonded allies in range. TalkHelper Talk-command helpers: who can talk to whom, and the vars a Talk event reads. Any adjacent live unit qualifies regardless of side — ally recruits and enemy parleys alike — so hosts gate specific pairs with Talk-trigger conditions (e.g. unit.nid == 'eirika' && unit2.nid == 'garcia' ). On acceptance hosts run recruit;unit2 (or any scripted effect). Pure: no mutation, no RNG. TalkHelper.CanTalk Pure adjacency+liveness predicate for one ordered pair (positions supplied by the caller so hosts can preview without moving tokens). public static bool CanTalk(Unit a, GridPoint posA, Unit b, GridPoint posB) Parameter Type Description a Unit First unit. posA GridPoint Tile of the first unit. b Unit Second unit. posB GridPoint Tile of the second unit. Returns: bool — True when both are alive and orthogonally adjacent. TalkHelper.TalkCandidates Every adjacent live placed unit (exclude self), in placement order. public static List<PlacedUnit> TalkCandidates(Battlefield field, PlacedUnit unit) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield holding placements. unit PlacedUnit Placed unit seeking conversation partners. Returns: List<PlacedUnit> — Adjacent live units in placement order. TalkHelper.TalkVars Vars for EventTrigger.Talk: unit (talker), unit2 (listener), position (the talker's tile) — same shape as BattleTriggers combat vars. public static Dictionary<string, object?> TalkVars(Unit talker, Unit listener, GridPoint position) Parameter Type Description talker Unit Unit initiating the talk. listener Unit Unit being talked to. position GridPoint Talker's tile. Returns: Dictionary<string, object?> — Vars dictionary for the Talk trigger. ThreatCalculator Danger-zone computation (Battlefield helper): ThreatRange per enemy and SideThreat union, optionally clipped by FogCalculator.VisibleTiles. Values are tile sets; callers supply movement and weapon range via LoadoutOf. ThreatCalculator.ThreatRange Danger zone for one enemy: attack rings over every tile it can reach. public static HashSet<GridPoint> ThreatRange(Battlefield field, PlacedUnit enemy, string movementGroup, int movePoints, int minRange, int maxRange) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield holding board and placements. enemy PlacedUnit Placed enemy whose threat is computed. movementGroup string Movement group key for reachability. movePoints int Movement allowance. minRange int Weapon minimum range. maxRange int Weapon maximum range. Returns: HashSet<GridPoint> — Every tile the enemy could strike. ThreatCalculator.LoadoutOf Resolves a unit's movement group, move allowance, and weapon ranges. public delegate (string group, int move, int minRange, int maxRange) LoadoutOf(PlacedUnit unit) Parameter Type Description unit PlacedUnit Placed unit whose loadout is requested. Returns: (string group, int move, int minRange, int maxRange) — Movement group, move allowance, minimum range, and maximum range. ThreatCalculator.SideThreat Unions threat ranges of many enemies, optionally clipped to sight. public static HashSet<GridPoint> SideThreat(Battlefield field, IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> enemies, LoadoutOf loadout, HashSet<GridPoint>? visibleOnly = null) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield holding board and placements. enemies IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> Enemies whose threat is unioned. loadout LoadoutOf Resolves each enemy's movement and range loadout. visibleOnly HashSet<GridPoint>? Optional visible set; threat outside it is dropped. Returns: HashSet<GridPoint> — Combined danger zone. ThreatCalculator.SideThreatValues Counts covering enemies per threatened tile. public static Dictionary<GridPoint, int> SideThreatValues(Battlefield field, IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> enemies, LoadoutOf loadout, HashSet<GridPoint>? visibleOnly = null) Parameter Type Description field Battlefield Battlefield holding board and placements. enemies IEnumerable<PlacedUnit> Enemies whose threat is counted. loadout LoadoutOf Resolves each enemy's movement and range loadout. visibleOnly HashSet<GridPoint>? Optional visible set; threat outside it is dropped. Returns: Dictionary<GridPoint, int> — Threat count per tile. TurnManager Phase cycler: teams act in list order, teams with no live units are skipped (player/index 0 never skipped), TurnNumber advances each time play returns to the first team. Win/loss is script-driven: events call SetResult (via win/lose commands) and the host polls BattleResult at event end. TurnManager.Teams Teams in phase order. public IReadOnlyList<string> Teams { get; } Type: IReadOnlyList<string> TurnManager.CurrentTeamIndex Index of the currently acting team. public int CurrentTeamIndex { get; private set; } Type: int TurnManager.CurrentTeam Currently acting team name. public string CurrentTeam => Teams[CurrentTeamIndex]; Type: string TurnManager.TurnNumber Round number (starts at 1, advances on return to the first team). public int TurnNumber { get; private set; } Type: int TurnManager.BattleResult null = ongoing, true = victory, false = defeat. public bool? BattleResult { get; private set; } Type: bool? TurnManager constructor Creates a phase cycler over the given team list. public TurnManager(IReadOnlyList<string> teams) Parameter Type Description teams IReadOnlyList<string> Team names in phase order (first entry is never skipped). TurnManager.SetResult Records the scripted win or loss flag. public void SetResult(bool won) Parameter Type Description won bool True for victory, false for defeat. TurnManager.Restore Restore saved progress (saves/turnwheel). Hosts only; Verify covers it. public void Restore(int teamIndex, int turnNumber, bool? battleResult) Parameter Type Description teamIndex int Saved acting-team index. turnNumber int Saved turn number. battleResult bool? Saved scripted result (null while ongoing). TurnManager.AdvancePhase Advances to the next live team, skipping empty teams except the first. public (string team, bool roundAdvanced) AdvancePhase(Func<string, bool> teamHasLiveUnits) Parameter Type Description teamHasLiveUnits Func<string, bool> Tests whether a team has live units. Returns: (string team, bool roundAdvanced) — New current team and whether a fresh round began (turn advanced).

title: Architecture
headings: What the core does not do
html:
Architecture

Namespaces

Namespace Responsibility Key types
Grid Board geometry and movement math Board, GridPoint, TerrainType, MovementGroups, RangeFinder
Data Definitions and live unit state Stats, UnitClass, Weapon, Unit, Chapter, StandardTerrains, TerrainEffects, Statuses, ClassDatabase, Promotion
Combat Battle math and resolution CombatRules, HitMode, WeaponTriangle, CombatResolver, SkillDef, SkillCatalog, SkillHook
Events Trigger/condition/command scripting EventTrigger, GameEvent, EventCommand, CommandCatalog, EventRunner, EventDispatcher, SimpleConditionEvaluator
Regions Named tile sets Region, RegionKind
Random Seeded determinism SeededRng
Tactics Chapter runtime: phases, objectives, AI TurnManager, Objectives, Battlefield, ThreatCalculator, EnemyAi, ChapterState, ChapterRunner, Experience, GrowthRates, SaveSystem, snapshots, FogCalculator, Rescue, SupportLedger

Dependencies flow one way: Tactics → Events/Combat/Data/Grid/Random. Grid and Random depend on nothing. Nothing references an engine.

Per-function reference with signatures, arguments, and returns (generated from source, see below): API: Grid, API: Data, API: Combat, API: Events, API: Regions, API: Random, API: Tactics.

// A host turn only ever calls downward: Tactics orchestrates, Combat/Data answer.
var range = field.Reachable(foe, foe.Unit.MovementGroup, foe.Unit.MovePoints); // Grid
CombatForecast fc = CombatResolver.Forecast(...);                              // Combat
CombatResult r = CombatResolver.Resolve(...);                                  // Combat
CombatGains.ApplyAfterCombat(...);                                             // Tactics over Data
PhaseTick.Apply(state, team);                                                  // Tactics over Data
EventDispatcher.Dispatch(trigger, vars, chapter.Events, runner);               // Events

Chapter runtime flow

Chapter (data) ──StartNew(seed)──▶ ChapterState
                                        │ Battlefield (placements)
                                        │ TurnManager (phases, turn #)
                                        │ CombatRng / GrowthRng (streams)
                                        │ Vars (level flags)
                                        ▼
loop: AdvancePhase ─▶ SpawnDue ─▶ player/AI actions ─▶ events ─▶ EvaluateObjectives
                                                            Ongoing / Victory / Defeat
  • Phases cycle team order, skipping teams with no live units; the turn counter advances each return to the first team.
  • Spawning deploys everything whose spawn turn has been reached (<=, never ==).
  • Actions use RangeFinder (move), CombatResolver (fight), EnemyAi (foes).
  • Events fire on triggers with conditions over trigger variables; win/lose commands set the scripted result.
  • Objectives are polled: scripted result first, then defeat specs, then victory specs.

What the core does not do

Rendering, animation, input, audio, file I/O, and networking are host concerns. The core exposes data (CombatForecast for the forecast window, HashSet<GridPoint> for range highlights and threat display) and interfaces (IEventExecutor) so any host — Unity, Godot, Blazor, a web front-end, or the headless ChapterRunner used in tests — can drive it. See hosting for worked examples.

title: Chapter format
html:
Chapter format

Chapters are single Markdown files (.md), one per chapter. MarkdownChapterLoader.Load(text, fileName) parses a file into a Chapter, collecting every error with file + line instead of failing fast.

Layout

# CH1: First Blood

## META
format: 1
objective: Rout the foe. Keep Eirika alive.
victory: rout
defeat: all_dead
defeat: protect eirika
next: ch2
maxDeploy: 4

## LEGEND

title: Chapter
html:
Chapter

Chapters can be authored as Markdown files — see chapter format (MarkdownChapterLoader), which parses boards, deployments, armory, regions, and events with file-and-line errors.

Definition vs runtime

  • Chapter is data: nid, title, board, deployments, regions, events, victory/defeat specs, armory, unit templates, MaxDeploy, formation region, next-chapter link.
  • ChapterState is the live run: battlefield, turn manager, two RNG streams, level vars, and spawn bookkeeping. StartNew(chapter, seed) deploys turn-1 units.

Lifecycle

  1. StartNew — turn-1 deployments appear; streams derive from the seed (CreateStream(seed, 0) for combat, (seed, 1) for growths).
  2. AdvancePhase + SpawnDue — after every phase advance, deploy everything whose spawn turn has been reached. The comparison is <=: jumping from turn 1 to turn 3 still spawns turn-2 reinforcements.
  3. Actions and events — movement, combat, AI, and trigger dispatch.
  4. EvaluateObjectives — scripted result first, then defeat specs, then victory specs; otherwise ongoing.

MaxDeploy caps turn-1 player deployments (0 means everyone); Validate flags over-deployment along with every other authoring error class.

// The canonical host lifecycle: open, step phases, close on outcome.
ChapterState state = ChapterState.StartNew(chapter, seed: 4242);
var runner = new ChapterRunner(state);
EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.LevelStart, new Dictionary<string, object?>(),
    chapter.Events, runner);

while (state.EvaluateObjectives() == ObjectiveOutcome.Ongoing) {
    state.Phases.AdvancePhase(team => TeamAlive(state, team));
    state.SpawnDue();
    PhaseTick.Apply(state, state.Phases.CurrentTeam);
    RunPhaseActions(state, runner); // movement, combat, AI, trigger dispatch
}

Headless runner

ChapterRunner implements IEventExecutor over a state so chapters play without a renderer — this is how chapters are tested today, and the same contract any host's presentation layer implements (see hosting):

Command Headless behavior
speak appended to the dialogue log
add_portrait, remove_portrait, wait recorded, no-op (presentation-only)
move_unit teleports the placed unit
spawn_unit clones the template, suffixing nids (brigand, brigand#2, …)
remove_unit extracts the placement
give_item adds the armory weapon to inventory
set_flag stores true/false in level vars
recruit / promote / heal / damage side flip, class rekey, HP swing
apply_status / clear_status / teach_skill status and skill bookkeeping
rescue / drop carry into Carried, drop back onto the map
equip / trade / drop_item / take_item reorder, swap adjacent, convoy stash/pull
visit / open once-only village flag, door/chest unlock (consumes key)
dance validates dancer skill, adjacency, and side; hosts refresh the target's turn
win / lose sets the scripted result

Every executed command is also appended to the stage log, giving a complete headless trace. Runtime failures (missing unit, template, or armory entry) throw — authoring errors must be loud, never silent. Passengers ride in Carried, stashed entries in Convoy, visited villages derive from Visited.

title: Combat
html:
Combat

Formulas follow GBA FE7/8 with tunables centralized in CombatRules (triangle bonuses, doubling threshold, hit mode, effective multiplier, TorchVisionBonus) — never scattered constants.

Forecast

CombatResolver.Forecast computes the battle-forecast window from attacker, weapon, defender, optional defender weapon, and terrain avoid/defense for both sides:

Value Formula
Damage max(0, Power + (effective ? Might×EffMult : Might) + triangle×MtBonus − Def/Res − terrainDef)
Hit clamp(Weapon.Hit + Skl×2 + Lck/2 + triangle×HitBonus − (foeAS + foeTerrainAvoid + foeLck/2))
Crit clamp(Skl/2 + Weapon.Crit − foeLck/2)
Strikes 2 when attacker AS exceeds defender AS by the threshold (default 4), else 1

Attack speed is Spd − max(0, Wt − Con). A disarmed defender's AS falls back to the attacker's weapon weight. Power covers Str or Mag; IsMagic selects Def vs Res.

// Forecast window, then the same numbers resolved for real.
CombatResolver.TerrainAt(board, atk.Position, out int atkAvo, out int atkDef);
CombatResolver.TerrainAt(board, def.Position, out int defAvo, out int defDef);
var (supHit, _) = supports.BonusFor(atk.Unit, atk.Position, field.Placed);
var (_, supAvoid) = supports.BonusFor(def.Unit, def.Position, field.Placed);

CombatForecast fc = CombatResolver.Forecast(
    atk.Unit, blade.Weapon, def.Unit, counter?.Weapon,
    atkAvo, atkDef, defAvo, defDef, rules,
    atk.Unit.Skills, def.Unit.Skills, supHit, supAvoid);

CombatResult result = CombatResolver.Resolve(
    atk.Unit, blade, def.Unit, counter, dist,
    atkAvo, atkDef, defAvo, defDef, state.CombatRng, rules,
    atk.Unit.Skills, def.Unit.Skills, supHit, supAvoid);

int dealt = 0;
foreach (CombatStrike s in result.Strikes)
    if (s.IsAttackerStrike && s.HitLanded) dealt += s.DamageDealt;
var (exp, levels) = CombatGains.ApplyAfterCombat(
    atk.Unit, def.Unit, dealt, !def.Unit.IsAlive,
    growths, state.GrowthRng, rules: null, usedWeapon: blade.Weapon);

Weapon triangle

Sword > Axe > Lance > Sword, and Anima > Light > Dark > Anima. Bows and staves sit outside. Advantage grants +1 might and +15 hit by default (GBA values, configurable). Without a defender weapon there is no triangle term.

Hit modes

Per-difficulty roll models (default 2RN):

Mode Behavior
Classic 1RN — single roll, true odds
TrueHit 2RN — mean of two rolls; high hit feels reliable, low hit hopeless
TrueHitPlus 3RN — mean of three rolls
Fates Single roll vs h + (40/3)(h/100)·sin((0.02h−1)·180°)

Rates <= 0 always miss and >= 100 always hit in every mode. Crit is always a single 1RN roll, and only rolled on a hit. Crits deal ×3 damage.

Effective damage

Weapon.EffectiveAgainst lists defender class keys (for example armor, flier). When it matches defender.ClassKey, might is multiplied by CombatRules.EffectiveMultiplier (default 3, GBA value) before the triangle term. Forecast.IsEffective reports the trigger. Chapter files add it as an armory token: effective:armor,flier.

Durability

InventoryEntry.UsesLeft is consumed by the InventoryEntry overload of CombatResolver.Resolve — 1 use per strike attempt, hit or miss, for attacker and counter. Broken entries (IsBroken) cannot strike. The Weapon overload stays pure (no durability) for forecasts and tests. Presentation layers should migrate to the entry overload instead of decrementing by hand (which missed counters).

Staves

Healing staves set HealPower (armory token heal:N) and usually type staff. ForecastHeal(healer, staff) previews HealPower + Power/2; ResolveHeal consumes 1 use, clamps to MaxHP, and returns HP restored.

Staves with accuracy use ForecastStaffHit(healer, staff, distance) — clamp(staff.Hit + Skl×2 + Lck/2 − 5/tile) — and ResolveStaff, which consumes 1 use and rolls 1RN (always 1RN, ignoring HitMode). Status staves set StatusEffect and StatusDuration (armory token status:sleep:2); on a hit the status is applied. IsStaff is true for staff type, positive heal power, or any status effect.

// Status staff at range: preview accuracy, then roll it for real (always 1RN).
int hit = CombatResolver.ForecastStaffHit(cleric, sleep.Weapon, dist);
bool landed = CombatResolver.ResolveStaff(cleric, sleep, patient, dist, state.CombatRng);
// On a hit the heal lands and/or Statuses.Apply runs; a use is spent either way.

Skills

Unit.Skills holds skill ids; hosts register effects in SkillCatalog as SkillDef records with a hook (OnAttack/OnDefense), flat forecast modifiers, and an optional ProcChance (1RN, rolled on the caller's proc RNG — pass null to preview without procs). ApplyToForecast returns an adjusted copy and never mutates the input, so forecast windows, AI scoring, and tests share the hook. Chapter files attach skills with the unit token skill:a,b (or skills:).

// Register once at load; ApplyToForecast never mutates its input.
SkillCatalog.Register(new SkillDef("brave-hit") { Hook = SkillHook.OnAttack, HitBonus = 20 });
SkillCatalog.Register(new SkillDef("guard") { Hook = SkillHook.OnDefense, DamageTakenPenalty = 2 });
CombatForecast mod = SkillCatalog.ApplyToForecast(baseFc, atk.Unit.Skills, def.Unit.Skills);
// Pass null procRng for previews; pass state.CombatRng to let ProcChance fire.

Forecast and both Resolve overloads take optional attackerSkills / defenderSkills lists (default null = unmodified) applied via ApplyToForecast with a null proc RNG — previews only, proc skills never fire mid-forecast. Resolve swaps the lists for the counter forecast, so the defender's OnAttack skills shape its counter and the attacker's OnDefense skills blunt it.

Support in battle math

Forecast and both Resolve overloads take optional supportHit / supportAvoid ints (default 0): supportHit is added to Hit, supportAvoid is subtracted as extra defender avoid, after skill mods. Hosts compute them from SupportLedger.BonusFor — the attacker's bonded hit bonus vs the defender's bonded avoid bonus — and swap the pair for the counter, exactly as the skill lists swap. EnemyAi.Decide accepts an optional SupportLedger and does this weighting itself for both the strike and the counter-risk forecast, alongside the units' own skills.

Experience gains

Tactics.CombatGains.ApplyAfterCombat(attacker, defender, damageDealt, didKill, growths, growthRng, rules?) wraps Experience.Gain + AddExp in one host call and returns (expGained, levelsGained) (levels counted by comparing Level before/after). Call it after Resolve with the summed damage dealt and the kill flag; same inputs + same growth seed always give the same level-ups. The trailing usedWeapon/wexpOnUse/wexpOnKill hook banks weapon experience too (see data): pass the fought weapon and the attacker gains wexpOnKill (default 3) on a kill, wexpOnUse (default 1) otherwise — omit it and no wexp moves.

Terrain lookup

CombatResolver.TerrainAt(board, pos, out avoid, out defense) is the single lookup for both sides. AI uses it via a TerrainOf delegate; UI forecast code should call it rather than hardcoding zeros.

Resolution order

CombatResolver.Resolve consumes the RNG and mutates HP: attacker strikes (possibly twice); a living defender whose weapon reaches the distance counters between the first and second strike. Same seed always replays identically — AI, forecasts, and tests share the function.

Post-strike unit actions live in Tactics.Dance (adjacent refresh) and Tactics.Canto (leftover-move repositioning) — both skill-gated, with hosts tracking acted flags. Experience and level-ups live in Tactics.Experience (granted via Tactics.CombatGains); statuses in Data.Statuses; support in Tactics.SupportLedger; see tactics.

Experience gains Tactics.CombatGains.ApplyAfterCombat(attacker, defender, damageDealt, didKill, growths, growthRng, rules?) wraps Experience.Gain + AddExp in one host call and returns (expGained, levelsGained) (levels counted by comparing Level before/after). Call it after Resolve with the summed damage dealt and the kill flag; same inputs + same growth seed always give the same level-ups. The trailing usedWeapon / wexpOnUse / wexpOnKill hook banks weapon experience too (see data ): pass the fought weapon and the attacker gains wexpOnKill (default 3) on a kill, wexpOnUse (default 1) otherwise — omit it and no wexp moves. Terrain lookup CombatResolver.TerrainAt(board, pos, out avoid, out defense) is the single lookup for both sides. AI uses it via a TerrainOf delegate; UI forecast code should call it rather than hardcoding zeros. Resolution order CombatResolver.Resolve consumes the RNG and mutates HP: attacker strikes (possibly twice); a living defender whose weapon reaches the distance counters between the first and second strike. Same seed always replays identically — AI, forecasts, and tests share the function. Post-strike unit actions live in Tactics.Dance (adjacent refresh) and Tactics.Canto (leftover-move repositioning) — both skill-gated, with hosts tracking acted flags. Experience and level-ups live in Tactics.Experience (granted via Tactics.CombatGains ); statuses in Data.Statuses ; support in Tactics.SupportLedger ; see tactics .

title: Data
html:
Data

Stats

GBA-style block: MaxHP, Power (covers Str or Mag — the weapon's IsMagic flag selects Def vs Res on the target), Skill, Speed, Luck, Defense, Resistance, Constitution (weapon-weight relief for attack speed).

Classes, weapons, units

  • UnitClass — key, name, MoveType, move points, optional promotion target.
  • Weapon — key, name, type, rank (E–S), might, hit, crit, weight, min/max range (Manhattan), max uses (durability), magic flag, EffectiveAgainst class tags, HealPower for staves. InRange(distance) tests a shot; IsStaff is true for staff type, positive heal power, or any status effect.
  • WeaponType — Sword, Lance, Axe, Bow, Anima, Light, Dark, Staff.
  • InventoryEntry — a weapon plus remaining uses; IsBroken at zero. Durability is consumed by the entry overload of CombatResolver.Resolve (1 use per strike attempt).
  • Unit — Nid (unique id used by events), name, side, class key, level, XP, current Stats, live HP, inventory, Vision (fog sight, default 5), Skills ids, Statuses (name → turns left), CarryingNid (rescue). Clone copies a unit for reinforcements.
  • Affiliation — Player, Enemy, Ally (NPC, own phase), Other (neutral, fights nobody).
// Build the pieces hosts own: units, weapons, classes, growths.
var sword = new Weapon("iron-sword", "Iron Sword", WeaponType.Sword, WeaponRank.E,
    might: 5, hit: 90, crit: 0, weight: 5, minRange: 1, maxRange: 1, maxUses: 40);
var eirika = new Unit("eirika", "Eirika", Affiliation.Player, "lord",
    new Stats { MaxHP = 18, Power = 4, Skill = 7, Speed = 8, Luck = 5,
                Defense = 3, Resistance = 2, Constitution = 5 });
eirika.Inventory.Add(new InventoryEntry(sword));
eirika.Skills.Add("brave-hit");          // SkillCatalog id, see combat
Statuses.Apply(eirika, "poison", 2);     // name -> turns left
WeaponRanks.AddWexp(eirika, WeaponType.Sword, 1);

var classes = new ClassDatabase();
classes.Add(new UnitClass("lord", "Lord", MoveType.Infantry, move: 6));
if (Promotion.CanPromote(eirika, classes))
    Promotion.Apply(eirika, "paladin", classes,
        gains: new Stats { MaxHP = 2, Power = 1 }); // per-class gains are host data

ClassDatabase maps class keys to UnitClass entries; see Promotion below.

Terrain set and effects

StandardTerrains.Create() returns GBA-flavored starter terrain (plain, road, bridge, forest, fort, village, gate, throne, mountain, water, wall). Forts heal 10% per round. Gameplay code depends only on TerrainType, so hosts can replace the set with their own data.

TerrainEffects.Apply(unit, terrain) applies the HP swing with ceiling rounding (any nonzero percent moves at least 1 HP), clamped to [0, MaxHP]. Callers decide timing; the convention is once per round per team at phase boundaries, not per activation.

Chapters

Deployment binds a unit to a tile, a spawn turn (default 1), and an optional group id. ObjectiveSpec factories read like design docs:

ObjectiveSpec.RoutEnemies()   // destroy every live Enemy unit
ObjectiveSpec.AllDead()       // defeat when no live Player unit remains
ObjectiveSpec.Survive(8)      // victory after completing 8 full rounds
ObjectiveSpec.Protect("eirika", "tana")
ObjectiveSpec.Seize("eirika", "gate")  // live eirika stands on region "gate"
ObjectiveSpec.EventOnly()     // win/lose commands decide; never auto-evaluated

Chapter bundles nid, title, board, deployments, regions, events, victory/defeat specs, an armory (weapons by key for give_item), unit templates (for spawn_unit), MaxDeploy (0 = everyone), formation region, and the next-chapter link.

Chapter.Validate() returns a list of authoring errors — off-board tiles, bad spawn turns, duplicate nids, over-deployment, unknown event verbs, unparsable conditions, and dangling protect tags — for the future editor to surface. A clean chapter validates to an empty list. At runtime, Tactics.DeploymentSelector.ChooseDeployments resolves a player-picked roster against the same deployments (MaxDeploy, formation regions) and reports selection errors without throwing.

Statuses

Data.Statuses manages Unit.Statuses: Apply, Has, Clear, and Tick (decrement all, drop expired, return expired names). Hosts tick at phase boundaries via Tactics.PhaseTick (which also deals poison damage and terrain swings), gate actions for sleep/silence themselves. Status staves apply through ResolveStaff.

Experience

Tactics.Experience is GBA-flavored and pure: Gain(kill, atkLvl, defLvl, damage) pays a chip base (10) or kill base (30) plus a capped level-difference bonus, plus (on non-kills only) a damage-based bonus of min(damageDealt, 20) / 4; AddExp banks toward 100 and calls LevelUp on overflow. LevelUp rolls 1RN per stat against GrowthRates on the growth RNG stream and heals MaxHP gains into CurrentHP. Tunables live in ExperienceRules. After combat, hosts grant through Tactics.CombatGains.ApplyAfterCombat, which returns (expGained, levelsGained).

Weapon experience

Data.WeaponRanks banks per-type wexp on Unit.Wexp (a WeaponType → points map, copied by Clone and saved/restored by SaveSystem): thresholds E 0, D 20, C 50, B 80, A 120, S 180. RankFor(points) reads the letter, PointsForRank(rank) the floor, CanEquip(points, rank) gates equipping, and AddWexp(unit, type, points) banks (returning the new total). Hosts grant through CombatGains.ApplyAfterCombat's trailing usedWeapon/wexpOnUse (default 1)/wexpOnKill (default 3) — pass the fought weapon and the attacker banks 1 per use, 3 per kill.

Promotion

ClassDatabase maps class keys to UnitClass entries (move type, move points, promotion target). Promotion.CanPromote checks the chain; Promotion.Apply rekeys ClassKey, adopts the new movement, and applies caller-supplied Stats gains (per-class GBA gains are host data). The promote;unit;class event verb rekeys only — full stat merges need the database on the host side.

title: Events
html:
Events

Trigger/condition/command scripting: every event is a unique name plus a trigger, a condition, and an ordered command list. Full member reference: API: Events.

Triggers

EventTrigger values and the vars each fires with:

Trigger Fires with vars
LevelStart, LevelEnd chapter open / close
PlayerPhaseStart, EnemyPhaseStart phase boundaries
UnitDeath unit nid, position
UnitWait, UnitSelect unit nid, position
UnitLevelUp unit nid
CombatStart, CombatEnd unit, unit2, item, position
Talk unit, unit2, position
Support unit, unit2, rank
RegionEntered unit, region, position

Commands

Text lines shaped verb;arg;arg (for example speak;Eirika;Oh no!). The catalog fixes each verb's arity (CommandCatalog):

Verb Args
speak speaker, text
add_portrait / remove_portrait unit; side for add
move_unit unit, x,y
spawn_unit template nid, faction, x,y
remove_unit unit
give_item unit, armory key
set_flag flag, true/false
recruit unit, optional faction (default player) — talk/recruit side flip
heal unit, amount — clamped to MaxHP
damage unit, amount — flat damage, floors at 0
promote unit, new class key — rekeys ClassKey
apply_status unit, name, optional duration (default 3)
clear_status unit, name
rescue carrier, passenger — pick up adjacent passenger
drop carrier, x,y — drop carried passenger adjacent
teach_skill unit, skill id
equip unit, weapon key — reorder that entry first (errors when missing)
trade giver, taker, weapon key — move the entry; the pair must be adjacent
drop_item unit, weapon key — stash the entry into the convoy
take_item unit, weapon key — pull the entry out of the convoy
gold amount — adjust party gold (negative spends; never below zero)
buy unit, weapon key — buy priced armory stock (price:N) into inventory
sell unit, weapon key — sell a carried entry for half price (floored)
visit unit — visit the village under the unit; once-only (sets visited_<name>)
open unit, x,y — open the adjacent door/chest at the tile; a locked one consumes the KeyId item from the opener (sets opened_<name>)
dance dancer, target — refresh an adjacent ally's turn (hosts clear acted flags)
shove shover, target — push adjacent target one tile away (Con ≤ shover Con+2, dest free)
swap a, b — swap positions of two adjacent units
steal thief, target, weapon key — steal adjacent light item when faster (weight ≤ thief Con)
warp unit, x,y — teleport if InBounds and not blocked
torch unit, amount — apply torch status 3 + Vision bump via CombatRules.TorchVisionBonus
win / lose (optional reason)
wait seconds (presentation timing)

Conditions

Tiny expression language for gating (SimpleConditionEvaluator): clauses joined by &&, each shaped path op literal with ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=. Paths resolve into nested dictionaries (unit.nid), literals are 'quoted', numbers, or true/false. Unknown paths are null and never equal a literal. Operators inside quotes are ignored, so name == 'a==b' splits correctly.

Running

EventRunner.Run checks the condition, validates every command up front, then dispatches in order — a broken verb fails before any side effect. EventDispatcher runs all same-trigger events by descending priority (then name), and stops at the first error. Effects reach the world only through IEventExecutor, which the headless ChapterRunner and each host's own presentation layer implement (see hosting).

// Author inline, run headless, or dispatch by trigger with vars.
var ev = new GameEvent("eirika-falls", EventTrigger.UnitDeath, "unit.nid == 'eirika'");
ev.AddCommand("speak;Seth;No!");
ev.AddCommand("lose;Eirika fell.");

var runner = new ChapterRunner(state);
EventRunResult once = EventRunner.Run(ev, vars, runner); // condition + validate + run

var deaths = EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.UnitDeath,
    new Dictionary<string, object?> {
        ["unit"] = new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["nid"] = "eirika" },
    }, chapter.Events, runner); // every matching event, priority first

title: Grid
html:
Grid

Coordinates

GridPoint is a zero-based immutable (X, Y) struct: X is the column (east), Y is the row (south). It offers Manhattan distance, value equality, and hashing, so it works as a dictionary key throughout the library.

Board

Board holds a terrain-key layout plus a terrain dictionary. It validates bounds and terrain keys on write, and throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException on out-of-bounds reads.

Board.FromRows authors maps from ASCII art:

var board = Board.FromRows(
    new[] { ".....", ".FF..", "..WT." },
    defaultTerrain: "plain",
    legend: new Dictionary<char, string> { ['.'] = "plain", ['F'] = "forest", ['W'] = "wall", ['T'] = "throne" },
    terrains: StandardTerrains.Create());

Rows must be rectangular; unknown glyphs throw FormatException with (x, y) coordinates. Legend keys are char (BMP glyphs only).

Terrain and movement groups

TerrainType carries per-group move costs, Avoid, Defense, and HpEffectPercent. Costs are keyed by movement-group name ("infantry", "armor", "cavalry", "flier", or any custom group such as "pirate"), so new movement types are data rows, not code branches. Unknown groups default to cost 1. Cost < 0 or >= 99 means impassable.

HpEffectPercent is the per-round HP swing as a percentage of max HP: positive heals, negative damages, zero does nothing (see data for application timing).

Range and path

RangeFinder provides three pure operations:

  • ComputeReachable — Dijkstra flood over tile-entry costs, returning each reachable tile mapped to movement points remaining on arrival. The blocked set excludes tiles (units); the origin is always allowed.
  • FindPath — A* with a Manhattan heuristic, returning the cheapest path within budget or null. The heuristic assumes per-tile costs stay >= 1; zero-cost custom terrain still yields a valid path but it may be suboptimal.
  • AttackTiles — the Manhattan ring between min and max range. Rendering and range checks share this one predicate so they can never diverge.

Both search overloads accept either a MoveType or a raw group name. The open list is a linear scan rather than a heap — maps are small and netstandard2.0 has no PriorityQueue; replace only with profiling evidence.

Example

// Movement range, path preview, and strike ring for one unit.
var blocked = field.BlockingTiles(unit);
var range = RangeFinder.ComputeReachable(
    board, unit.Position, unit.MovePoints, unit.MovementGroup, blocked);
foreach (var tile in range.Keys) Highlight(tile); // tile -> move remaining

var path = RangeFinder.FindPath(
    board, unit.Position, cursor, unit.MovePoints, unit.MovementGroup, blocked);
if (path != null) Animate(path); // cheapest route within budget, null if unreachable

var ring = RangeFinder.AttackTiles(board, unit.Position, sword.MinRange, sword.MaxRange);
bool canStrike = ring.Contains(foe.Position);

Blocking rule

Exactly one rule, enforced in Battlefield: enemies block pass-through; allies are pass-through but cannot be landed on.

title: Hosting
html:
Hosting

SrpgCore has no engine references (netstandard2.0, no packages), so every host follows the same shape: reference the library, keep presentation in thin adapters, and call the same pure functions the Verify suite covers. The four examples below — Unity, Godot, Blazor, and a framework-agnostic web client — show that shape across very different runtimes; none of them is the design center, and a new host follows the same rules.

Shared mapping (all hosts)

Concern Core API Host job
Board + movement Board, RangeFinder, Battlefield.Reachable tilemap render, range highlights, path preview
Forecast UI CombatResolver.Forecast, TerrainAt forecast window, effective/triangle badges
Combat Resolve entry overload (durability), ResolveHeal attack animation, HP bars, break icons
AI EnemyAi.Decide with TerrainOf/DefenderWeaponOf enemy turn driver, threat overlay via ThreatCalculator
Events EventRunner/EventDispatcher + IEventExecutor dialogue boxes, portraits, movement tweens
Objectives ChapterState.EvaluateObjectives banners, game-over screens
Fog FogCalculator + Unit.Vision hide tokens, gate targeting
Rescue Rescue + rescue;/drop; carry/drop animations, laden move display
Skills SkillCatalog.ApplyToForecast skill icons, proc flashes
Support SupportLedger.BonusFor bond UI, adjusted forecast
Statuses Data.Statuses + status staves status icons, phase-boundary ticks
Saves SaveSystem DTOs file/localStorage/cloud persistence

1) Unity

  • Reference: drop the built SrpgCore.dll under Assets/Plugins/ (auto-referenced). No source port, no package install.
  • Data: author chapters as the same Markdown files and load at runtime with MarkdownChapterLoader.Load (via Resources/StreamingAssets), or convert armory, classes, and growths into ScriptableObject DBs that feed Weapon/UnitClass/ GrowthRates constructors. ClassDatabase maps directly to a class-table asset.
  • Turn driver: a ChapterController : MonoBehaviour owns the ChapterState, cycles TurnManager, and runs coroutines per phase: highlight Battlefield.Reachable, animate RangeFinder.FindPath, call Resolve, then CombatGains.ApplyAfterCombat, PhaseTick.Apply at phase boundaries, and EvaluateObjectives after every checkpoint.
// Thin Unity adapter: the core decides, coroutines animate.
public sealed class ChapterController : MonoBehaviour {
    ChapterState _state = null!;
    ChapterRunner _runner = null!;

    void Start() {
        var loaded = MarkdownChapterLoader.Load(chapterText.text, "ch1.md");
        _state = ChapterState.StartNew(loaded.Chapter!, (uint)Random.Range(1, int.MaxValue));
        _runner = new ChapterRunner(_state);
        EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.LevelStart,
            new Dictionary<string, object?>(), _state.Chapter.Events, _runner);
    }

    IEnumerator Strike(PlacedUnit atk, InventoryEntry blade, PlacedUnit def) {
        // ... forecast panel via CombatResolver.Forecast, attack animation ...
        CombatResult r = CombatResolver.Resolve(atk.Unit, blade, def.Unit, counter,
            atk.Position.ManhattanDistance(def.Position),
            0, 0, 0, 0, _state.CombatRng);
        yield return AnimateStrikes(r); // HP bars follow result.AttackerHPLeft/DefenderHPLeft
    }
}
  • Events: implement IEventExecutor with TextMeshPro dialogue, portrait Sprite swaps, and DOTween/Animator movement for move_unit. recruit/promote flip side/class and swap prefabs; heal/damage drive floating numbers.
  • Saves: serialize ChapterSnapshot with JsonUtility (or JSON.NET) to Application.persistentDataPath; armory keys are the contract, so renames need migration. RNG states round-trip, so suspend/resume continues the same sequence.
  • Why it fits: Unity's prefab/UI/anim systems cover exactly what the core omits (rendering, input, audio), and C# means zero interop cost.

2) Godot

  • Reference: Godot's C# build is an ordinary MSBuild SDK project, so SrpgCore.csproj goes straight into the generated .csproj as a normal <ProjectReference> (or the built DLL as a <Reference>) — no plugin-folder convention to work around, unlike engines that compile scripts out of band.
  • Data: load the same Markdown chapters with MarkdownChapterLoader.Load, reading the text via FileAccess.GetFileAsString("res://chapters/ch1.md"); armory/classes can stay as the same Markdown-defined data or move into custom Godot Resource/.tres assets that feed the Weapon/UnitClass constructors.
  • Turn driver: a ChapterController : Node owns ChapterState and ChapterRunner. Godot C# has no Unity-style coroutines, so phase sequencing uses async/await with scene-tree timers instead:
// Thin Godot adapter: async/await replaces Unity's coroutines for sequencing.
public partial class ChapterController : Node {
    ChapterState _state = null!;
    ChapterRunner _runner = null!;

    public override void _Ready() {
        var text = FileAccess.GetFileAsString("res://chapters/ch1.md");
        var loaded = MarkdownChapterLoader.Load(text, "ch1.md");
        _state = ChapterState.StartNew(loaded.Chapter!, (uint)GD.Randi());
        _runner = new ChapterRunner(_state);
        EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.LevelStart,
            new Dictionary<string, object?>(), _state.Chapter.Events, _runner);
    }

    async Task Strike(PlacedUnit atk, InventoryEntry blade, PlacedUnit def, InventoryEntry? counter) {
        CombatResult r = CombatResolver.Resolve(atk.Unit, blade, def.Unit, counter,
            atk.Position.ManhattanDistance(def.Position),
            0, 0, 0, 0, _state.CombatRng);
        await ToSignal(GetTree().CreateTimer(0.6), SceneTreeTimer.SignalName.Timeout);
        RefreshHud(r); // HP bars follow result.AttackerHPLeft/DefenderHPLeft
    }
}
  • Events: implement IEventExecutor over Label/RichTextLabel dialogue and AnimationPlayer/Tween movement for move_unit; emit a Godot [Signal] per command so UI nodes can react without the controller knowing about them directly.
  • Saves: serialize ChapterSnapshot with System.Text.Json and write it through FileAccess.Open("user://save.json", FileAccess.ModeFlags.Write) — user:// resolves to the platform save directory the same way across desktop and console exports.
  • Why it fits: Godot's node/signal composition maps cleanly onto IEventExecutor, and its .NET build treats SrpgCore like any other project reference rather than needing a special asset-folder route.

3) Blazor

Blazor is the one host shape where the "logic" and the "UI" are both C# running in the same process — in WebAssembly, that process is the browser tab itself, so there is no network hop and no serialization boundary between a player action and a core call.

  • Reference: a normal <ProjectReference> in the Blazor project's .csproj, same as any other .NET library — netstandard2.0 is binary-compatible with the WASM runtime, so this needs no adapter project at all.
  • Data: ship chapter Markdown as static web assets (wwwroot/chapters/ch1.md), fetch with HttpClient, and parse with MarkdownChapterLoader.Load.
  • State: a scoped DI service holds ChapterState/ChapterRunner so razor components share one turn loop instead of each re-deriving it:
// Scoped service: the one ChapterState/ChapterRunner every component reads.
public sealed class ChapterStateService {
    public ChapterState State { get; private set; } = null!;
    public ChapterRunner Runner { get; private set; } = null!;
    public event Action? Changed;

    public async Task LoadAsync(HttpClient http, uint seed) {
        var text = await http.GetStringAsync("chapters/ch1.md");
        var loaded = MarkdownChapterLoader.Load(text, "ch1.md");
        State = ChapterState.StartNew(loaded.Chapter!, seed);
        Runner = new ChapterRunner(State);
        Changed?.Invoke();
    }

    public void Strike(PlacedUnit atk, InventoryEntry blade, PlacedUnit def, InventoryEntry? counter) {
        CombatResolver.Resolve(atk.Unit, blade, def.Unit, counter,
            atk.Position.ManhattanDistance(def.Position), 0, 0, 0, 0, State.CombatRng);
        Changed?.Invoke(); // a .razor component calls StateHasChanged() on this
    }
}
  • Rendering: a .razor component lays the Board out as a CSS grid of elements, calling RangeFinder.ComputeReachable and CombatResolver.Forecast directly from click handlers — the forecast panel reads straight off the same objects the combat call will use, with nothing to keep in sync.
  • Events: IEventExecutor mutates component-bindable state (dialogue text, portrait id) and raises ChapterStateService.Changed, which components forward to StateHasChanged().
  • Saves: WebAssembly has no filesystem, so persist through IJSRuntime: serialize SaveSystem.Save(state) with System.Text.Json and call JSRuntime.InvokeVoidAsync("localStorage.setItem", key, json); Restore on load.
  • Blazor Server: the same service/component code also runs unchanged under Blazor Server — the core still executes in one C# process, it is just the server process instead of the browser, with the UI mirrored down over SignalR. Pick this shape over WebAssembly when you want the RNG and save data to never leave the server.
  • Why it fits: no other host here skips the serialization boundary entirely — the forecast a player sees and the Resolve call that follows it touch the exact same Unit/Weapon instances.

4) Framework-agnostic web client

Logic server + JS frontend, for when the UI is owned by a non-.NET framework instead of Razor. Host the core in a minimal ASP.NET API (or a headless dotnet worker): endpoints for reachable tiles, forecasts, AI moves, event runs, and save blobs. The client stays rendering-only — grid canvas, threat overlay, forecast panel, dialogue queue — and mirrors its movement/combat/ai/events modules against the server as oracle. SaveSystem DTOs cross as JSON; SeededRng states make replays and spectator links trivial (?seed=…&turn=…). Keep the TS side behavior-locked with vectors copied from Verify (forecast hand-computed values, 2RN bands, <= reinforcement spawns) so the web build cannot drift from the core.

// Logic server (minimal API): numbers stay in C#, the browser only renders.
app.MapPost("/forecast", (ForecastRequest q) => {
    CombatResolver.TerrainAt(board, q.From, out int aAvo, out int aDef);
    CombatResolver.TerrainAt(board, q.To, out int dAvo, out int dDef);
    return CombatResolver.Forecast(q.Attacker, q.Weapon, q.Defender, q.Counter,
        aAvo, aDef, dAvo, dDef);
});
app.MapGet("/range", (int x, int y, int move, string group) =>
    RangeFinder.ComputeReachable(board, new GridPoint(x, y), move, group));
app.MapPost("/saves", (ChapterSnapshot snap) => store.Save(snap)); // SaveSystem DTO as JSON

Non-goals for hosts

No host duplicates core math (triangle, hit modes, XP, growths, threat). New verbs need a CommandCatalog entry plus executor handling on every host, plus a Verify check — the same rule as the core.

title: Overview
html:
Overview

SrpgCore is an engine-agnostic Fire Emblem-style SRPG core library in C#. Pure logic — grid, data, combat, events, tactics, chapters — with no rendering, no engine API, and no third-party packages. It targets netstandard2.0 so the same assembly runs under Unity, Godot, Blazor, Flax, Prowl, or any other .NET host.

Design rules

  • Deterministic. One seeded RNG stream per concern (combat, growths). Same seed + same inputs always give the same battle, so forecasts, AI, replays, and tests share one code path. No wall-clock reads, no static mutable state.
  • Pure where it matters. Forecasts, ranges, paths, and objective checks are pure functions. Anything that touches the outside world (dialogue, movement animation, spawning visuals) sits behind an interface such as IEventExecutor.
  • Data over code. Movement groups, terrain costs, hit modes, and formula tunables are data or config. New unit types and terrain need no code changes.
  • Fail fast for authors. Map glyphs, event verbs, chapter references, and conditions are validated with positions and names, never silently ignored.

Repository layout

SrpgCore lives in its own project, separate from any engine host:

Location Contents
SrpgCore/ The library (Grid, Data, Combat, Events, Regions, Random, Tactics)
SrpgCore.Verify/ Offline console verifier, no test packages — run anywhere dotnet exists
SrpgCore.slnx Solution for this project only

Engine hosts are separate sibling projects that reference the built library — see hosting for how Unity, Godot, Blazor, and web clients each pull it in. None of them vendors or duplicates this source.

Commands

dotnet build SrpgCore.slnx
dotnet run --project SrpgCore.Verify/SrpgCore.Verify.csproj

The verifier runs 463 checks across grid, RNG, combat, events, phases, objectives, AI, chapters, durability/effectiveness, experience, staves, new event verbs, terrain-aware AI, seize, saves, promotion, fog, rescue, skills, support, statuses, staff accuracy, combat gains, skill/support battle math, battle triggers, phase tick, deployment selection, talk, inventory verbs, interactables, weapon ranks, ally AI, fog-filtered threat/AI, AI tie-breaks, dance, canto, shove/swap/steal/healer/hold/regen/convoy/support-tick/replay-hash, warp/torch, set_terrain, MaxInventory, ReversesTriangle, FormationRegion, BecomesTerrainKey, shop gold/buy/sell, and exits non-zero on failure.

Sixty-second battle

using SrpgCore.Combat; using SrpgCore.Data; using SrpgCore.Grid; using SrpgCore.Tactics;

var terrains = StandardTerrains.Create();
var board = Board.FromRows(new[] { ".....", ".FF..", "..WT." }, "plain",
    new Dictionary<char, string> { ['.'] = "plain", ['F'] = "forest", ['W'] = "wall", ['T'] = "throne" },
    terrains);
var sword = new Weapon("iron-sword", "Iron Sword", WeaponType.Sword, WeaponRank.E,
    might: 5, hit: 90, crit: 0, weight: 5, minRange: 1, maxRange: 1, maxUses: 40);
var atk = new Unit("hero", "Hero", Affiliation.Player, "mercenary",
    new Stats { MaxHP = 20, Power = 5, Skill = 6, Speed = 7, Luck = 3, Defense = 4, Resistance = 1, Constitution = 8 });
var blade = new InventoryEntry(sword);
atk.Inventory.Add(blade);

var rng = new SeededRng(42); // or ChapterState.StartNew(chapter, seed).CombatRng
CombatForecast fc = CombatResolver.Forecast(atk, sword, foe, null, 0, 0, 0, 0);
CombatResult result = CombatResolver.Resolve(atk, blade, foe, null, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, rng);
