title: Tactics
html:
Tactics

Phases

TurnManager cycles a team list in order (default player, enemy, ally, other). Teams with no live units are skipped — except the first team, which is never skipped. TurnNumber starts at 1 and advances each time play returns to the first team, so "survive N" means completing N full rounds. SetResult records a scripted win/lose flag that EvaluateObjectives honors before any computed check.

// One phase step of the canonical host loop.
bool TeamAlive(string t) => state.Field.Placed.Any(p => p.Unit.IsAlive && TeamOf(p.Unit.Side) == t);
var (team, wrapped) = state.Phases.AdvancePhase(TeamAlive);
state.SpawnDue();                 // <= comparison: skipped turns still reinforce
PhaseTick.Apply(state, team);     // terrain + poison + status tick for that team
switch (state.EvaluateObjectives()) {
    case ObjectiveOutcome.Victory: /* banner, campaign advance */ break;
    case ObjectiveOutcome.Defeat:   /* game over */ break;
}

Objectives

Spec Met when
Rout(side) no live unit of that side remains
Survive(n) TurnNumber > n
Protect(tags) a listed nid is dead and already spawned
Seize(unit, region) that live unit stands on that region
EventOnly never — win/lose commands decide

The protect rule needs emphasis: future spawns (spawnTurn > turn) never trip it, and the spawn comparison is <=, so a skipped turn number can neither drop a reinforcement nor a protection check. Poll defeat specs before victory specs, and poll after every elimination checkpoint (post-combat, turn end).

Battlefield and threat

Battlefield holds the board plus placements and answers occupancy questions: LiveEnemiesOf, BlockingTiles (live hostiles), AllyTiles (live non-hostiles). Hostility: Player and Ally fight the Enemy; Other fights nobody.

ThreatCalculator.ThreatRange unions every enemy's attack ring over every tile it can reach — the danger zone for "show all threats" UI and defensive scoring. Like GBA games, tiles adjacent to an enemy count as threatened even when impassable; tiles no reachable position can strike stay out.

Enemy AI

EnemyAi.Decide is greedy, in three steps:

  1. Strike in place. If any usable weapon reaches any foe from the current tile, take the best shot — no movement.
  2. Move, then strike. Score every (tile, weapon, target) triple and take the best landable tile.
  3. Approach. Otherwise walk the reachable tile nearest to the closest foe; if already closest, wait.

Healer priority runs first: if a heal staff can reach a wounded ally (staff range from any reachable tile, fog-aware), the most-missing-HP ally is healed (move included). Otherwise scoring prefers secured kills (10000 + damage) over expected damage (damage × hit% + 2 × damage × crit%), minus CounterWeight × expected counter damage when a defender weapon is known (default weight 0.5 in the terrain-aware overload; the legacy overload ignores counters). Pass a TerrainOf lookup (usually CombatResolver.TerrainAt over the board) so fort/throne defense and avoid shape picks; pass a DefenderWeaponOf selector or the AI falls back to the foe's first in-range weapon. Ties break toward least movement spent, then nearest target, then coordinate order — never RNG or hash order. Every usable (unbroken) weapon is considered. Pass an optional SupportLedger to weight bonded hit/avoid bonuses into the strike forecast and (swapped) into the counter-risk forecast; the units' own Skills always shape both forecasts via the same hook as CombatResolver. Staff behavior is future work.

EnemyAi.TerrainOf terrainOf = (u, t) => {
    CombatResolver.TerrainAt(field.Board, t, out int avo, out int def);
    return (avo, def);
};
AiAction act = EnemyAi.Decide(field, foe, foe.Unit.MovementGroup,
    Rescue.EffectiveMove(foe.Unit), terrainOf,
    defenderWeaponOf: null, counterWeight: 0.5, rules: null,
    supports: ledger, visibleTiles: FogCalculator.VisibleTiles(field, foe.Unit.Side));
if (act.IsWait) { /* end unit */ }
else {
    if (act.MoveTo != null) MoveToken(foe, act.MoveTo.Value);
    if (act.Target != null) Strike(foe, act.Weapon!, act.Target);
}

Battle triggers

BattleTriggers builds the vars dictionaries hosts hand to EventDispatcher — pure, no mutation, shaped for the condition language (unit.nid, position.x/y):

Helper Trigger Vars
CombatStartVars(attacker, defender, weaponKey, pos) CombatStart unit, unit2, item, position
CombatEndVars(..., defenderDied) CombatEnd above plus defender_died
LevelUpVars(unit) UnitLevelUp unit (nid, level, hp)
UnitWaitVars(unit, pos) UnitWait unit, position
DetectRegionEntries(placed, previousPositions, regions) RegionEntered one (unit, region, pos) per true entry

DetectRegionEntries reports only false→true region transitions: units that stayed put, left a region, or have no previous position (fresh spawns) never report. See BattleTriggers.DetectRegionEntries for the exact shapes.

// Around one exchange: announce it, resolve it, announce the result.
EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.CombatStart,
    BattleTriggers.CombatStartVars(atk.Unit, def.Unit, blade.Weapon.Key, atk.Position),
    chapter.Events, runner);
CombatResult result = CombatResolver.Resolve(...);
EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.CombatEnd,
    BattleTriggers.CombatEndVars(atk.Unit, def.Unit, blade.Weapon.Key, atk.Position,
        defenderDied: !def.Unit.IsAlive),
    chapter.Events, runner);
if (levelsGained > 0)
    EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.UnitLevelUp,
        BattleTriggers.LevelUpVars(atk.Unit), chapter.Events, runner);

// After movement: snapshot positions before, compare after.
var before = field.Placed.ToDictionary(p => p.Unit.Nid, p => p.Position);
... move tokens ...
foreach (var (unit, region, pos) in BattleTriggers.DetectRegionEntries(field.Placed, before, chapter.Regions))
    EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.RegionEntered,
        new Dictionary<string, object?> {
            ["unit"] = new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["nid"] = unit.Unit.Nid },
            ["region"] = region.Name,
            ["position"] = new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["x"] = pos.X, ["y"] = pos.Y },
        }, chapter.Events, runner);

Talk

TalkHelper finds adjacent conversation partners: TalkCandidates(field, unit) lists every adjacent live placed unit of any side (ally recruits and enemy parleys alike — hosts gate pairs with Talk-trigger conditions), CanTalk(a, posA, b, posB) is the pure adjacency+liveness predicate, and TalkVars(talker, listener, talkerPos) builds the unit/unit2/position vars for EventTrigger.Talk. On acceptance hosts run recruit;unit2 (or any scripted effect).

// Talk menu for the selected unit; pair gating lives in event conditions.
foreach (PlacedUnit other in TalkHelper.TalkCandidates(field, selected))
    ShowTalkOption(other); // e.g. enabled when a Talk event matches the pair
// On accept:
EventDispatcher.Dispatch(EventTrigger.Talk,
    TalkHelper.TalkVars(selected.Unit, other.Unit, selected.Position),
    chapter.Events, runner); // conditions like unit.nid == 'eirika' && unit2.nid == 'garcia'

Interactables

Chapter.Interactables holds doors, chests, and villages placed on the map; Validate checks in-bounds tiles and duplicate names, and the chapter format adds an INTERACTABLES section. At runtime the headless ChapterRunner drives them with visit;unit (must stand on an unvisited village; once-only, recorded as Vars["visited_<name>"] so hosts fire village events once) and open;unit;x,y (opener adjacent to a closed door/chest; a locked one needs the KeyId item in the opener's inventory and consumes it; recorded as Vars["opened_<name>"] plus the data-side Opened mirror). The runner holds no extra state beyond Vars — Visited derives the visited names from it, so saves round-trip everything.

Ally AI and fog-aware targeting

AllyAi.Decide is the EnemyAi greedy loop with counterWeight 0.25 instead of the enemy default 0.5 — GBA greens wade in and discount counter-risk. Hosts call it for Ally-side units on the ally phase. Both it and the enemy terrain-aware Decide take an optional visibleTiles set: foes outside it are skipped entirely (targeting and approach), so blind units wait instead of sniping the unseen. ThreatCalculator.SideThreat takes an optional visibleOnly set that drops threat tiles outside sight — pass FogCalculator.VisibleTiles through both to keep AI and danger zones honest in fog.

Dance and canto

Post-strike unit actions, both skill-gated (skill:dance / skill:canto on the markdown unit row, matched case-insensitively, no catalog registration needed). The core holds no acted flags — hosts own exhaustion state; Tactics.Dance and Tactics.Canto are the shared legality predicates so every host grants the same moves.

Dance.CanDance(dancer, target) needs a living skilled dancer adjacent to a living non-hostile target that isn't itself (CheckDance is the throwing validator). The dance;dancer;target event verb enforces the same rules and fails fast headlessly; on success hosts clear their acted flag for the target and mark the dancer acted.

Canto.CanCanto(unit, moveTotal, moveSpentBeforeAction) needs the skill plus unspent move; Canto.RemainingMove is the leftover (total - spent, clamped at 0, negatives throw). Pass laden totals through Rescue.EffectiveMove.

// Dancer's turn: shared legality check, then the host flips its own acted flags.
Dance.CheckDance(dancer, ally); // throws when illegal (skill, range, side, liveness)
ClearActed(ally.Unit.Nid);
MarkActed(dancer.Unit.Nid);

// Rider attacks, then spends whatever move is left (laden totals via Rescue).
int total = Rescue.EffectiveMove(rider.Unit);
if (Canto.CanCanto(rider.Unit, total, spentBeforeAttack))
    AllowMove(rider, Canto.RemainingMove(total, spentBeforeAttack));

Shove, swap, and steal

Shove.CanShove/ExecuteShove pushes an adjacent target one tile away when target.Con ≤ shover.Con + 2 and the destination is in-bounds and vacant; Shove.CanSwap/ExecuteSwap swaps two adjacent live units. Steal.CanSteal/Execute steals a light item when adjacent, thief Speed > target Speed, Weapon.CanSteal true, and Weight ≤ thief.Con. Verbs shove;, swap;, steal; enforce the same rules headlessly.

Support tick and AI types

SupportLedger.TickAdjacent grants 1 point per adjacent alive pair; Unit.AiType (rush default, hold never moves, patrol pings between PatrolA/PatrolB) gates EnemyAi.Decide. ReplayHash.Compute hashes placements+HP+RNG for deterministic replay checks. Statuses.IsSilenced blocks staff/magic; ChapterRunner equip now enforces WeaponRanks.CanEquip; convoy aliases ChapterState.Convoy so saves round-trip.

Phase tick

PhaseTick.Apply(state, team, rules?) runs upkeep for one team at its phase boundary, in deterministic X-then-Y tile order: terrain HP swing (TerrainEffects.Apply), then poison damage (PoisonDamage, default 3) for units with the poison status, then Statuses.Tick. Returns per-unit (nid, hpDelta, expiredStatuses). Ticks never kill — a unit alive at tick start is left at 1 HP minimum. PhaseTickRules toggles each step (PoisonDamage, TickStatuses, ApplyTerrain).

Deployment picker

DeploymentSelector.ChooseDeployments(chapter, nids) resolves a requested roster against the chapter's deployments and returns (chosen, errors) without throwing: unknown nids error, MaxDeploy is enforced when positive, and when any Formation-kind region exists each pick must stand inside one. Hosts surface the errors in the deployment screen.

var (chosen, errors) = DeploymentSelector.ChooseDeployments(chapter, requestedNids);
if (errors.Count > 0) ShowDeploymentErrors(errors); // unknown nid, MaxDeploy, formation
else StartChapter(chosen);

Experience

Kills and chips feed Experience.Gain / AddExp / LevelUp on the growth RNG stream; see data. Hosts grant XP after combat via CombatGains.ApplyAfterCombat, which returns (expGained, levelsGained) — the headless runner itself still never auto-grants.

Saves

SaveSystem.Save(state) snapshots positions, HP, level/XP, inventory uses, turn and phase index, vars, and both RNG states. Restore(chapter, snap, baseSeed) rebuilds an equivalent state; armory keys are the save contract (missing keys throw), and already-placed deployments are marked so SpawnDue never duplicates. DTOs are plain data — hosts serialize with whatever they have (System.Text.Json, Unity JsonUtility, localStorage). Snapshots now include vision, skills, statuses, and rescue state.

// Suspend/resume (or turnwheel): snapshot, serialize with your stack, restore.
ChapterSnapshot snap = SaveSystem.Save(state);
File.WriteAllText(slot, JsonSerializer.Serialize(snap)); // host's serializer
ChapterState back = SaveSystem.Restore(chapter,
    JsonSerializer.Deserialize<ChapterSnapshot>(File.ReadAllText(slot))!, seed);

Fog

FogCalculator.VisibleTiles(field, side) unions Manhattan balls of radius Unit.Vision over live units of that side; HiddenEnemiesOf lists live foes outside it. No line-of-sight blocking — walls cost movement but not sight. Hosts hide tokens, skip threat from hidden units, and gate targeting on visibility.

var seen = FogCalculator.VisibleTiles(field, Affiliation.Player);
tokenRenderer.SetVisible(foe, seen.Contains(foe.Position));
var danger = ThreatCalculator.SideThreat(field, enemies, LoadoutOf, visibleOnly: seen);

Rescue

Rescue.CanGrab/Grab/Drop implement GBA-simplified carry: adjacent grab when the carrier's hands are free and passenger Con fits (<= carrier Con + 2), one passenger at a time, laden move halved (EffectiveMove), passenger off-map while carried (untargetable — hosts hide the token). Event verbs rescue;/drop; drive it; the headless runner holds passengers in Carried.

if (Rescue.CanGrab(pegasus.Unit, eirika.Unit, pegasus.Position, eirika.Position))
    Rescue.Grab(field, pegasus, eirika); // passenger token leaves the map
int move = Rescue.EffectiveMove(pegasus.Unit); // halved while laden
Rescue.Drop(field, pegasus, eirika.Unit, tile); // tile must be adjacent and free

Support

SupportLedger tracks points per unit pair and ranks them C (30) / B (80) / A (150). BonusFor grants +5 hit/avoid per rank step per bonded ally within 3 tiles (C +5, B +10, A +15). Pure over placements — add the returned bonus to forecast hit and avoid on both sides before display and AI scoring.

ledger.AddPoints("eirika", "seth", 80); // rank B
var (hit, avoid) = ledger.BonusFor(eirika, eirikaPos, field.Placed);
// hit/avoid feed Forecast/Resolve supportHit/supportAvoid (see combat).
text: Tactics Phases TurnManager cycles a team list in order (default player, enemy, ally, other ). Teams with no live units are skipped — except the first team, which is never skipped. TurnNumber starts at 1 and advances each time play returns to the first team, so "survive N" means completing N full rounds. SetResult records a scripted win/lose flag that EvaluateObjectives honors before any computed check. // One phase step of the canonical host loop. bool TeamAlive(string t) => state.Field.Placed.Any(p => p.Unit.IsAlive && TeamOf(p.Unit.Side) == t); var (team, wrapped) = state.Phases.AdvancePhase(TeamAlive); state.SpawnDue(); // <= comparison: skipped turns still reinforce PhaseTick.Apply(state, team); // terrain + poison + status tick for that team switch (state.EvaluateObjectives()) { case ObjectiveOutcome.Victory: /* banner, campaign advance */ break; case ObjectiveOutcome.Defeat: /* game over */ break; } Objectives Spec Met when Rout(side) no live unit of that side remains Survive(n) TurnNumber > n Protect(tags) a listed nid is dead and already spawned Seize(unit, region) that live unit stands on that region EventOnly never — win / lose commands decide The protect rule needs emphasis: future spawns ( spawnTurn > turn ) never trip it, and the spawn comparison is <= , so a skipped turn number can neither drop a reinforcement nor a protection check. Poll defeat specs before victory specs, and poll after every elimination checkpoint (post-combat, turn end). Battlefield and threat Battlefield holds the board plus placements and answers occupancy questions: LiveEnemiesOf , BlockingTiles (live hostiles), AllyTiles (live non-hostiles). Hostility: Player and Ally fight the Enemy; Other fights nobody. ThreatCalculator.ThreatRange unions every enemy's attack ring over every tile it can reach — the danger zone for "show all threats" UI and defensive scoring. Like GBA games, tiles adjacent to an enemy count as threatened even when impassable; tiles no reachable position can strike stay out. Enemy AI EnemyAi.Decide is greedy, in three steps: Strike in place. If any usable weapon reaches any foe from the current tile, take the best shot — no movement. Move, then strike. Score every (tile, weapon, target) triple and take the best landable tile. Approach. Otherwise walk the reachable tile nearest to the closest foe; if already closest, wait. Healer priority runs first: if a heal staff can reach a wounded ally (staff range from any reachable tile, fog-aware), the most-missing-HP ally is healed (move included). Otherwise scoring prefers secured kills ( 10000 + damage ) over expected damage ( damage × hit% + 2 × damage × crit% ), minus CounterWeight × expected counter damage when a defender weapon is known (default weight 0.5 in the terrain-aware overload; the legacy overload ignores counters). Pass a TerrainOf lookup (usually CombatResolver.TerrainAt over the board) so fort/throne defense and avoid shape picks; pass a DefenderWeaponOf selector or the AI falls back to the foe's first in-range weapon. Ties break toward least movement spent, then nearest target, then coordinate order — never RNG or hash order. Every usable (unbroken) weapon is considered. Pass an optional SupportLedger to weight bonded hit/avoid bonuses into the strike forecast and (swapped) into the counter-risk forecast; the units' own Skills always shape both forecasts via the same hook as CombatResolver . Staff behavior is future work.
